findings.location: lib/core/sync/sync_engine.dart:133-151 (esp. the `for (final answer in pending)` loop at 140-144); lib/core/sync/media_upload_coordinator.dart:108-119 (esp. the `for (final row in rows)` loop at 112-115)
findings.evidence: `_flush`/`scanAll` only check `_backoff.isActive` once, at the top of the method, before the loop starts. Once `_flushOne`/`_advance` catches a `RateLimitException` for one row mid-loop (registering the cooldown via `_backoff.registerRateLimited`), the loop does not re-check `_backoff.isActive` and keeps calling `_flushOne`/`_advance` for every remaining row in the same pass. Two consequences: (1) every remaining row in the pass still fires a doomed request during an active 429 burst instead of being skipped, and (2) because `RateLimitBackoff._nextInterval()` doubles `_lastInterval` on every call to `registerRateLimited`, a single pass that rate-limits on N rows compounds the exponential growth N times in one tick (e.g. two 429s in the same pass jump straight to 2s/4s instead of a single 1s step), rather than growing by one step per genuine retry cycle.
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 7's own Design Constraint (b) and Success Criteria explicitly require the backoff to suppress the *entire* flush/scan pass, not just the offending row ("retrying every pending row again... only worsens the burst"). The current code satisfies this only across passes (the next tick correctly no-ops via the top-of-method `isActive` check) but not within the pass that first hits the 429 — it keeps hammering the same rate-limited endpoint for every other pending row, and distorts the intended 1s->2s->4s exponential curve into an uncontrolled multi-step jump whenever more than one row is rate-limited in the same tick. This can leave the client backed off far longer than the real 429 signal warranted, or continue sending doomed requests during an active burst.
findings.required_action: Inside `_flush`'s and `scanAll`'s loops, check `_backoff.isActive` after each row/answer and break out of the loop as soon as it becomes true (or check it before each iteration), so a 429 encountered partway through a pass stops the rest of that pass immediately instead of letting every remaining row also attempt and re-register the backoff.

findings.evidence: Both call sites execute the identical 5-line terminal-teardown sequence in the same order: `_attemptPublicId = null; _syncEngine.setActiveTask(null); _syncEngine.stopSync(); _timerService.stop(); _mediaUploadCoordinator.stop(); emit(AttemptCompleted(attemptPublicId));` — copy-pasted rather than extracted into one shared private method.
findings.why_it_matters: This phase's Design Constraint explicitly states force-submit must reach 'the same terminal AttemptCompleted state and teardown sequence... as the natural end-of-tasks path' — which the code does today, but by duplicating the sequence verbatim rather than sharing it. Any future change to the teardown (e.g. adding `_syncEngine.dispose()`, cancelling a new subscription, or emitting an additional side effect) has to be made in both places; missing one is a silent behavioral drift between the two 'same outcome' paths this phase's own contract says must stay identical.
findings.required_action: Extract the shared teardown+emit sequence into one private helper (e.g. `_completeAttempt(String attemptPublicId, Emitter<ExamAttemptState> emit)`) and call it from both `_onForceSubmitRequested` and `_emitFromResponse`.
